answer: With a Hardware security key bound by signed confirmation letter with one identity per channel, the account is only as strong as its binding: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the signed confirmation letter is recorded, and one identity per channel keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. One zephyr proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of bindings. A pearl and a horizon may look alike, but only the identity with a verified channel is honoured.
